evals.name: task-manager-classic
evals.prompt: I want to build a Task Manager application in Form.io. Projects have Tasks assigned to them. I want to assign users to projects, where each user only has access to the Tasks within their Project. Plan the resources for me.
evals.expected_output: Phase B writes the artifact pair template.md + template.json (paired basenames, paired collision timestamps). template.md has top-level `# Resource Map` title and sections in order: Resources, Users & Auth, Roles, Access Matrix, ER Diagram, Access Flow Diagram, Companion artifact. Resources include Project, Task, User, and at least one join (ProjectUser) with a Group Assignment action. Access Matrix table includes rows for administrator (all/all/all/all) and authenticated (group-based on Project/Task, own on ProjectUser). ER Diagram and Access Flow Diagram both contain ASCII bodies (not just headings). template.json top-level keys title/name/description/version/roles/resources/forms/actions all present; default roles administrator, authenticated, anonymous all defined. Chat output renders the markdown block first, then the JSON block, then the one-line filename confirmation, then the Next Steps block.

evals.name: crm-with-company-scoping
evals.prompt: Help me design a simple CRM in Form.io. Sales reps should be able to see Contacts and Deals, but only the ones belonging to Companies they're assigned to. A Contact belongs to one Company. A Deal belongs to one Company and can have multiple Contacts attached. We want self-register for reps with email/password, and an Admin role that sees everything.
evals.expected_output: Phase B writes template.md + template.json pair. template.md has all required sections in order. Resources include Company, Contact, Deal, plus at least one join (DealContact for N:N, plus CompanyUser for rep-to-company group access). Access Matrix rows reflect group-via-CompanyUser on Company/Contact/Deal, admin-all, sales rep owns their CompanyUser rows. Access Flow Diagram shows the CompanyUser Group Assignment writing the ACL onto Company, then field-based inheritance onto Contact and Deal. Self-register form carries Role Assignment. template.json defines roles administrator + authenticated + anonymous at minimum.

evals.name: minimal-no-auth-feedback
evals.prompt: I want a super simple public feedback form for my website. Anyone can submit feedback (name, email, message). I don't want users, accounts, or logins. Can you plan this in Form.io?
evals.expected_output: Phase B writes template.md + template.json pair. template.md Users & Auth section states 'None. App is public.' (or equivalent). Resources: a single Feedback resource/form with three fields (name textfield, email email, message textarea). Access Matrix has a single row: anonymous create_all, no read. Access Flow Diagram collapses to the one-line anonymous form. NO Group Assignment / Group Permissions action anywhere in template.json. No join resources. Roles section keeps the default three Form.io roles for completeness.

evals.name: complex-crm-transitive
evals.prompt: I want to build a full CRM in Form.io. The company uses Teams — each sales rep belongs to one or more Teams, and each Team owns a set of Accounts. Under each Account there are Contacts (people at the company), Deals (sales opportunities), and Activities (calls, emails, meetings, tasks). An Activity can optionally be tied to a specific Deal. Accounts also have a primary contact. Sales reps should only see data (Accounts, Contacts, Deals, Activities) belonging to Teams they are members of. Admins see everything. Self-register with email/password.
evals.expected_output: Phase B writes template.md + template.json pair. template.md has all required sections in order. Seven resources: User (default), Team (the group), TeamUser (join with Group Assignment action: group=team, user=user), Account (direct child of Team with 'team' select carrying field-based submissionAccess), Contact (grandchild — account select + hidden calculated 'team' mirror with submissionAccess), Deal (same mirror pattern), Activity (same mirror pattern + optional deal ref). Access Matrix rows distinguish administrator (all/all/all/all everywhere) from salesRep (group/group/group/— on Account/Contact/Deal/Activity). Access Flow Diagram calls out the transitive mirror propagation — TeamUser → Team → Account (direct) → Contact/Deal/Activity (via hidden calc mirror). template.json: every grandchild has at least one hidden component whose calculateValue is exactly `value = data.<parent>?.data?.team || value;` (both halves of the guard — no unguarded `data.<parent>.data.team`). Two forms: userLogin, userRegister. Roles: administrator, salesRep, authenticated, anonymous. Phase B template.json is importable.

evals.name: change-time-entries
evals.prompt: My Task Manager project already exists in Form.io. Its current template is the baseline at `packages/skill-tests/evals/formio-resource-planner/fixtures/baseline-task-manager/template.json`, and its `template.md` is in the outputs directory you were given. I also want to track time entries on tasks: each entry records the hours worked and the date, belongs to one task, and is logged by the signed-in user. Members of a project should see and log time on that project's tasks, the same way they see the tasks. Plan this change.
evals.expected_output: Change mode: template.md is updated in place with a `## Change — <date> — <title>` section; changes.json is written (no template.json). changes.json creates a `timeEntry` resource with a select referencing the baseline `task` resource, a `timeEntry:save` action, and the group access that reaches it (a hidden calculated mirror of the project, since it sits two levels below the group). It repeats no baseline role, resource, form, or action, carries no top-level `access`, and lists any change to existing forms under `updates`.

evals.name: change-vendor-on-deals
evals.prompt: My CRM project already exists in Form.io. Its current template is the baseline at `packages/skill-tests/evals/formio-resource-planner/fixtures/baseline-crm/template.json`, and its `template.md` is in the outputs directory you were given. Add vendors: a Vendor has a name and a contact email, and administrators maintain the vendor list in the portal while sales reps can read it. Each existing Deal should be able to reference one vendor. Plan this change.
evals.expected_output: Change mode: template.md is updated in place with a `## Change — <date> — <title>` section; changes.json is written (no template.json). changes.json creates a `vendor` resource with a `vendor:save` action and read access for salesRep, and an `updates` entry for the baseline `deal` resource adding a select whose `data.resource` is `vendor`. It repeats no baseline role, resource, form, or action and carries no top-level `access`.
